definition: A neural network in which information flows in one direction, from input to output, without cycles.
details: In transformer blocks, position-wise feedforward networks are applied after the attention layer to further transform each token's representation.

explainer.lead: A feedforward neural network processes information in one direction, from input to output, with no loops back to earlier parts. This straightforward structure also appears inside transformer blocks, where a position-wise network refines each token after attention.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a conveyor belt that carries information through several worktables, always moving forward and never circling back. Each table changes the information a little before passing it on. In a transformer, this happens separately for each word-like token after the token has gone through attention.
tiers.practitioner: In a transformer block, apply the position-wise feedforward network after attention to transform each token representation. The network has no recurrent connections, so it does not itself route information back through time or earlier activations. Keep its role distinct from attention: attention supplies the preceding contextual processing, while the feedforward stage further transforms each position.
tiers.paperLevel: A feedforward neural network is a directed acyclic computation mapping an input x to an output y, with no cyclic information flow. In a transformer block, the position-wise form computes h'_i = FFN(h_i) for each token position i after attention. Its defining structural limit is the absence of feedback cycles.

components.name: Directed processing layers
components.detail: Successive transformations pass information toward the output without feeding it back through a cycle.

components.name: Output
components.detail: The final transformed representation produced by the forward computation.

components.name: Position-wise application
components.detail: In transformer blocks, the feedforward network transforms each token's representation after the attention layer.

flow: An input representation enters the network.
Directed processing stages transform it and pass it forward, without cycles.
The network emits its output representation.
In a transformer block, attention runs first and the position-wise feedforward network then transforms each token representation.
explainer.lineage: Position-wise feedforward networks are a component of transformer blocks, following attention and further transforming token representations.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a simple one-way computation for transforming representations and serves as a distinct processing stage inside transformer blocks.
